task: Task 1 — headline evals on the 4 golden states (AZ, CA, CO, TX)

supersedes.reason: Deployed detections were corrupted: els-detection-batch-preparer-role-dev lacked bedrock:InvokeModel, so Pass-1 depth-map inference failed with AccessDeniedException, an empty {} depth map was persisted, and every detection batch ran in no-depth-map mode. Fixed in infra/cdk/lib/pipeline-stack.ts (BedrockInvokeAccess + CloudWatchMetricsAccess on DetectionBatchPreparerLambdaRole), deployed 2026-07-17. The 07-16 reports are retained as depth-map-off ablation evidence for Task 3.

inputs.extraction_equivalence_note: outputs/07-17-26 extraction files are byte-identical in text payload to outputs/07-16-26-2 (they differ only in source_version_id and extraction_timestamp; SHA-256 of the payload with those two keys removed matches for all four states). The detector eval therefore consumed the same input in both sessions.

commands_in_order: # 0. gate check: confirm the run post-dates the deploy and the depth map worked (CO ~65 elements / 0 sub_strands = fixed; 93 with sub_strands = pre-fix)
# 1. fresh no-cache runs against the post-fix outputs folder
# 2. variance probe on the two states whose recall moved (3 fresh same-session runs each)

AWS_PROFILE=kinder-readiness-dev-cli python -m evaluation.eval_detector --extraction-dir outputs/07-17-26 --state CO --state TX --no-cache --stability-runs 3 --report-json paper/results/task1_detector_stability_CO_TX.json
# 3. consolidation (consolidate_task1.py is now path-parameterized; defaults reproduce the base-name files)
caveats: DETECTOR OUTPUT IS NOT REPRODUCIBLE ACROSS SESSIONS (headline methodological caveat, finding 1): the 07-16 and 07-18 detector evals ran on byte-identical extraction text with identical detector code and produced materially different detections - AZ 66 vs 64 elements, CA 122 vs 122 (identical sequence), CO 65 vs 63, TX 28 vs 37. Recall consequently moved CO 0.857->1.000 and TX 0.750->1.000 with no code or input change. A single-run recall figure is not a reportable point estimate in either direction; report a range or mean+/-spread over N>=3 time-separated sessions. The 07-16 run's three 'genuine detector defects' (CO strand title-fusion, TX-IND-02-PK3 truncation, TX-IND-02-PK4 drop) did not recur and were samples, not defects.

THE SUITE'S --stability-runs IS AN INADEQUATE VARIANCE INSTRUMENT AND MUST NOT BE CITED AS EVIDENCE OF DETERMINISM: it reported level-disagreement 0.000 / size-stdev 0.00 for CO and TX (3 genuine no-cache runs) in the same session in which a 24h-separated run differed by up to 9 elements. Two defects: (a) it samples only within one session; (b) measure_stability keys elements on (code, title) and counts a disagreement only when a matched pair differs in level, so title truncation/fusion - the failure mode actually observed - drops out of the comparison rather than counting against stability.

PRECISION IS ANNOTATION-COVERAGE-BOUNDED, NOT A HALLUCINATION RATE: the detector goldens are partial spot-checks (AZ 5, CA 25, CO 7, TX 8 elements) while the detector emits 9-122 elements inside annotated domains. Every unmatched in-annotated-domain detection counts as a false positive even when it is correct document content (verified by inspection: all 5 AZ 'false positives' are real unannotated document elements). Ceiling precision from coverage alone this run: AZ 5/9, CA 25/122, CO 7/44, TX 8/29. Do not report raw precision as detector quality in the paper.

THE SUITE'S LEVEL-CONFUSION MATRIX IS STRUCTURALLY DIAGONAL: level is part of the match key (both domain-scoped and fallback), so a level-misclassified element can never pair with its golden; misclassifications surface as one FN plus one FP instead. paper/analysis/consolidate_task1.py computes a level-agnostic confusion analysis for the paper: 0 off-diagonal in all four states in both the 07-16 and 07-18 runs. The eval_detector module docstring ('precision/recall on (level, code) tuples') is also stale: matching is code-agnostic on (domain, level, title, age_band).

MATCHING IS TITLE-EXACT AFTER WHITESPACE/CASE NORMALIZATION: this is why title-fidelity variance (fused definitions, truncation) shows up as recall misses. Fairly counted as misses, but see the reproducibility caveat - whether a given title defect appears is run-dependent.

PARSER FIELD ACCURACY INCLUDES UPSTREAM EXTRACTION NOISE: AZ's field mismatches are all single-space word fusions from Textract extraction (e.g. 'firmfoundation', 'andphysical') surviving into descriptions, not hierarchy errors. AZ fully_correct=0 is entirely attributable to this (sub_strand.description 0.278, indicator.description 0.667, domain.description 0.722).

PARSER INPUT PATH RESOLVED: batched (deployed) and direct-path detections now converge for CO - both give 9/9 coverage and n_parsed=48 (batched field-acc 0.994 / 8 fully-correct vs direct 0.969 / 7, a gap within run-to-run variance). The paper may take parser numbers from the deployed batched path. task1_parser_CO_on_direct_detection.json is retained as the direct half of this comparison.

DOMAIN-AGNOSTIC FALLBACK MATCHING: eval_detector falls back to (level, title, age_band) matching when domain-scoped lookup misses. Before the CA golden reorder fix this silently cross-matched 5 CA elements across FLD/ELD domains; after the fix, 0. AZ's out-of-domain golden indicator (AZ-IND-LL-1-2-b, annotated without its Language and Literacy domain header) still relies on this fallback, and its domain is excluded from precision scoping while the indicator itself counts toward recall.

GOLDEN DATA FIXES APPLIED DURING TASK 1 (both verified score-neutral or transcription-error corrections, never matcher loosening): (1) CA detector golden: FLD Grammar/Sharing/Participating block (doc pages 7-8) was listed after the ELD entries, breaking document-order domain tagging - reordered to true document order; (2) TX parser golden: duplicated test_case_id TX-IND-04-PK4 - first entry (indicator VI.A.1, doc page 7) had source_page 9, fixed to 7; second entry (indicator VI.A.4) had strand.code IV.A, a transposition typo for VI.A (TX Science is domain VI), fixed, and re-id'd as TX-IND-05-PK4.

OPEN GOLDEN-CONVENTION QUESTION (not fixed, needs Emily's call): TX parser golden expects indicator.description=None for TX-IND-03/04/05 but the parser emits the child-behavior outcome text as the description (indicator.description accuracy 0.500 for TX). Whether TX indicator descriptions should be empty is an annotation-convention decision; graded as genuine mismatches for now.

DEPTH-MAP GRADING is a per-state exact-match on the canonical-level sequence (a boolean, not a percentage), computed standalone by calling infer_depth_map on the full extraction blocks - same call shape as production detect_structure. All four states PASS in both runs.
CORPUS TIER: every number in task1_* files is from the _only_subset tier (9-15pp manually trimmed subset PDFs), never full documents.
